I will do it much like I did in recent years, with some small adjustment if input prices move too much. On my 9 mu, wheat and maize are one after another on the same land, so I count both crops on the full 9 mu. I have only 2 people at home, so I will keep the work simple and use what I know works here. Around Quzhou, if wheat is short of fertilizer, the heads stay small, and if maize is hungry at jointing, the ears do not fill well. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key times instead of gambling on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer, water it several times, and spray 2 times if disease and aphids show up. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give it more nitrogen than wheat, water at the main stages, and spray 2 times for weeds and insects if needed. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and money compared with deep ploughing every season, and on 9 mu that is what fits my family best.
